name: Gothic Lolita
eras: 2000s international spread via visual kei bands and magazines like Gothic & Lolita Bible

media.title: Gothic & Lolita Bible (magazine, launched 2001)
media.note: the main print vehicle that spread the look globally

media.title: Mana (Malice Mizer, visual kei musician)
media.note: widely credited with popularizing the elegant-gothic-lolita strand

reacts_against: the exposed, Western-coded sexiness of mainstream fashion; Gothic Lolita deliberately covers the body in historical silhouette as a form of modesty-as-style.
revivals: steady subcultural continuity rather than a single revival; renewed international visibility via 2020s J-fashion YouTube/TikTok

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Crosses, bats, religious iconography, chandeliers, castles, coffins, deep red roses
wiki_facts.key_colours: Black, white, deep jewel tones (maroon, navy, crimson, purple)
wiki_facts.related_aesthetics: AristocratClassic LolitaGothLolitaRomantic GothSweet LolitaVictorianVictorian GothVisual Kei
wiki_facts.key_values: Elegance, darkness, mystery, drama, Victorian-era aesthetics

findings: dark — about 42% of the measured color across 6 wiki images is below mid-lightness
mostly muted — about 73% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Aesthetics Wiki photos as photographed and displayed on screen; actual garments and materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
